docs.title: 🐍 Python Fundamentals — Cheat Sheet
docs.text: Covers: Videos 001–010 (Week 01)

docs.title: 📌 Syntax Basics
docs.text:
# This is a comment
print("Hello, World!")  # Your first Python program

"""
This is a multi-line comment
(actually a docstring)
"""
Concept Example Print to console print("Hello") Single-line comment # comment here Multi-line comment """ ... """ or ''' ... ''' End of statement Newline (no ; needed) Code blocks Indentation (4 spaces)

docs.title: 📌 Data Types Overview
Rules for Variable Names
docs.text: ✅ Valid ❌ Invalid Why my_name my-name No hyphens _private 2fast Can't start with a number camelCase my name No spaces CONSTANT class Can't use reserved keywords

docs.title: Declaration & Assignment
docs.text:
# Single assignment
name = "Fady"
age = 22
is_student = True

# Multiple assignment
x, y, z = 1, 2, 3

# Same value to multiple variables
a = b = c = 0

# Swap values
x, y = y, x

docs.title: Naming Conventions
docs.text:
# Variables & functions → snake_case
user_name = "fady"
def calculate_total():
    pass

# Constants → UPPER_SNAKE_CASE
MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3
PI = 3.14159

# Classes → PascalCase
class MyClass:
    pass

docs.title: 📌 Escape Sequences
docs.text:
Sequence Output Description \n Newline Moves to next line \t Tab Horizontal tab \\ \ Backslash \' ' Single quote \" " Double quote \r Carriage return Goes to line start \b Backspace Removes previous char \0 Null Null character 
print("Line 1\nLine 2")
# Line 1
# Line 2

print("Name:\tFady")
# Name:   Fady

print("He said \"Hello\"")
# He said "Hello"

# Raw string — ignores escape sequences
print(r"C:\Users\new_folder")
# C:\Users\new_folder

docs.title: 📌 String Concatenation
docs.text:
# Using + operator
first = "Hello"
last = "World"
full = first + " " + last  # "Hello World"

# Using * for repetition
line = "-" * 20  # "--------------------"

# f-strings (formatted strings) — preferred!
name = "Fady"
age = 22
print(f"My name is {name} and I'm {age} years old")

# You CANNOT concatenate str + int directly
# print("Age: " + 22)  # ❌ TypeError
print("Age: " + str(22))  # ✅ "Age: 22"

docs.title: 💡 Common Pitfalls
docs.text: Mistake Fix print "Hello" print("Hello") — need parentheses in Python 3 "age: " + 25 "age: " + str(25) or f"age: {25}" Name = "A" then using name Python is case-sensitive! Forgetting indentation Always use 4 spaces for blocks

docs.title: 🧠 Quick Quiz
docs.text:
1. What does type(3.14) return? → <class 'float'>
  2. Is my_var a valid variable name? → ✅ Yes
  3. What does \t do? → Inserts a horizontal tab
  4. How to repeat a string 3 times? → "abc" * 3 → "abcabcabc"
  5. What's the output of print("A" + "B" + "C")? → ABC

docs.text: Covers: Videos 011–015 (Week 02, partial)

docs.title: 📌 Creating Strings
docs.text:
# Single or double quotes
s1 = 'Hello'
s2 = "World"

# Multi-line strings
s3 = """This is a
multi-line string"""

s4 = '''Also works
with single quotes'''

# Empty string
empty = ""

docs.title: 📌 String Indexing
docs.text:
Strings are zero-indexed — each character has a position:

 H   e   l   l   o
 0   1   2   3   4      ← positive index
-5  -4  -3  -2  -1      ← negative index

word = "Hello"
word[0]    # 'H'   — first character
word[4]    # 'o'   — last character
word[-1]   # 'o'   — last (from end)
word[-2]   # 'l'   — second to last

docs.title: 📌 String Slicing
docs.text:
Syntax: string[start:end:step]

Slice Result Explanation s[0:3] "Hel" Index 0, 1, 2 (end is exclusive) s[:3] "Hel" From start to index 2 s[2:] "llo" From index 2 to end s[:] "Hello" Full copy s[::2] "Hlo" Every 2nd character s[::-1] "olleH" Reversed string s[-3:] "llo" Last 3 characters s[1:4] "ell" Index 1, 2, 3 
text = "Python Programming"

# Extract "Python"
text[:6]        # "Python"

# Extract "Programming"
text[7:]        # "Programming"

# Reverse the string
text[::-1]      # "gnimmargorP nohtyP"

# Every other character
text[::2]       # "Pto rgamn"

docs.title: Case Methods
docs.text: Method Example Result .upper() "hello".upper() "HELLO" .lower() "HELLO".lower() "hello" .title() "hello world".title() "Hello World" .capitalize() "hello world".capitalize() "Hello world" .swapcase() "Hello".swapcase() "hELLO"

docs.title: Search Methods
docs.text: Method Example Result .find(sub) "Hello".find("ll") 2 (index) .find(sub) "Hello".find("xyz") -1 (not found) .index(sub) "Hello".index("ll") 2 (index) .index(sub) "Hello".index("xyz") ValueError ❌ .count(sub) "hello".count("l") 2 .startswith() "Hello".startswith("He") True .endswith() "Hello".endswith("lo") True

docs.title: Whitespace & Padding
docs.text: Method Example Result .strip() " hi ".strip() "hi" .lstrip() " hi ".lstrip() "hi " .rstrip() " hi ".rstrip() " hi" .center(10) "hi".center(10, "-") "----hi----" .ljust(10) "hi".ljust(10, "-") "hi--------" .rjust(10) "hi".rjust(10, "-") "--------hi" .zfill(5) "42".zfill(5) "00042"

docs.title: Modify & Replace
docs.text: Method Example Result .replace(a, b) "Hello".replace("l", "r") "Herro" .split() "a b c".split() ["a", "b", "c"] .split(",") "a,b,c".split(",") ["a", "b", "c"] .join() "-".join(["a","b"]) "a-b" .expandtabs(4) "a\tb".expandtabs(4) "a b"

docs.title: Check / Validate
docs.text: Method Returns True when... .isalpha() All characters are letters .isdigit() All characters are digits .isalnum() All characters are letters or digits .isspace() All characters are whitespace .isupper() All cased characters are uppercase .islower() All cased characters are lowercase .istitle() String is in title case

docs.title: 📌 String Properties
docs.text:
s = "Hello"

# Strings are IMMUTABLE — you can't change them in place
# s[0] = "h"  # ❌ TypeError

# Length
len(s)         # 5

# Membership
"ell" in s     # True
"xyz" not in s # True

# Iteration
for char in s:
    print(char)  # H, e, l, l, o

docs.title: 📌 Key Differences
docs.text: .find() vs .index() .find("x") → returns -1 if not found .index("x") → raises ValueError if not found .strip() variants .strip() → removes from both sides .lstrip() → removes from left only .rstrip() → removes from right only

docs.title: 💡 Common Pitfalls
docs.text: Mistake Fix s[0] = "h" Strings are immutable! Use s = "h" + s[1:] s.upper() then expecting s changed Methods return new strings: s = s.upper() s.split("") Can't split on empty string — use list(s) instead Off-by-one in slicing Remember: s[start:end] — end is exclusive

docs.title: 🧠 Quick Quiz
docs.text:
1. What does "Python"[1:4] return? → "yth"
  2. How to reverse "abc"? → "abc"[::-1] → "cba"
  3. Difference between .find() and .index()? → .find() returns -1, .index() raises error
  4. Is "hello".upper() destructive? → No, returns new string
  5. What does "a-b-c".split("-") return? → ["a", "b", "c"]

docs.title: Philosophy
docs.text:
Every 5 videos = 1 project

These projects are designed to:

  1. Apply the exact concepts from the videos you just watched
  2. Build something tangible you can show off
  3. Reinforce learning through hands-on practice
  4. Stay fun — no boring exercises, only real programs!

As you progress through the course, new projects will be added automatically.

docs.title: 📊 Web Dashboard
docs.text: A beautiful, interactive progress dashboard for tracking your Python course journey.

docs.title: How to Open
docs.text:
Simply open the file in your browser:

# From the repository root
start dashboard/index.html     # Windows
open dashboard/index.html      # macOS
xdg-open dashboard/index.html  # Linux

Or double-click dashboard/index.html in your file explorer.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• 🎯 Animated progress rings for videos, study plan, and assignments
  • 📚 Collapsible week cards showing all 15 weeks and their lessons
  • ✅ Per-lesson status tracking (done / pending)
  • ⚡ Quick access links to cheatsheets, projects, flashcards, and CLI
  • 🌙 Dark theme with glassmorphism design
  • 📱 Fully responsive — works on mobile and desktop
  • ⚡ Zero dependencies — pure HTML/CSS/JS, no build step

docs.title: Updating Progress
docs.text: To update your progress, edit the weeks array in dashboard/index.html and change done: false to done: true for completed lessons.

docs.title: 🧠 Flashcard System
docs.text: A CLI-based spaced repetition flashcard tool to test and reinforce your Python knowledge.

docs.title: How to Run
docs.text:
# Interactive menu
python flashcards/flashcards.py

# Load a specific deck
python flashcards/flashcards.py --deck 01

# List available decks
python flashcards/flashcards.py --list

docs.title: Available Decks
docs.text: Deck Topic Cards 01_fundamentals Syntax, variables, data types 20 02_strings Indexing, slicing, string methods 20

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• 🃏 Shuffled cards — different order every time
  • 💡 Hints — optional hints for each question
  • 📝 Explanations — learn why the answer is correct
  • 📊 Score tracking — see your results and progress over time
  • 🎯 Smart matching — partial answer matching for long answers
  • 💾 Persistent scores — your history is saved to .scores.json

docs.title: Adding Your Own Decks
docs.text:
Create a JSON file in flashcards/decks/ with this format:

{
  "id": "my_deck",
  "name": "My Custom Deck",
  "description": "Description here",
  "cards": [
    {
      "question": "What is Python?",
      "answer": "A programming language",
      "hint": "Named after Monty Python",
      "explanation": "Python is a high-level language."
    }
  ]
}
